newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says new feed import rule may be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says new feed import rule may be delayed.

text.p: New regulations on feed raw material imports, which remove import quotas and cut tariffs, are set to be delayed beyond the scheduled November 1 deadline, Deputy Commerce Minister Montri Danpaiboon said Wednesday.
He told reporters that it might take two to three months from now for any tariff cut to actually take effect because the finance ministry might take that long to issue a decree.

The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved the food policy committee's proposal to lift import quotas and cut import duty on feed ingredients such as soybean, soymeal and maize, with effect from November 1.
"Even though that was the date set by the government, in practice importers might face some problems due to bureaucracy in the customs department," Montri said.
